fields.author: George Orwell
fields.description: 1984 is a dystopian novel by George Orwell published in 1949. Set in a totalitarian society ruled by Big Brother, it follows Winston Smith as he secretly rebels against the oppressive Party that controls every aspect of life.

fields.title: The Alchemist
fields.author: Paulo Coelho
fields.description: The Alchemist is a novel by Paulo Coelho that follows Santiago, a young Andalusian shepherd who dreams of finding treasure near the Egyptian pyramids. Along the way he discovers the importance of following his dreams.

fields.title: The Hunger Games
fields.author: Suzanne Collins
fields.description: The Hunger Games is a dystopian novel by Suzanne Collins set in a future North America called Panem. Sixteen-year-old Katniss Everdeen volunteers to take her sister's place in a televised death match between children.

fields.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
fields.author: Gabriel Garcia Marquez
fields.description: One Hundred Years of Solitude is a landmark novel by Gabriel Garcia Marquez that tells the multi-generational story of the Buendia family in the fictional town of Macondo, blending reality with magical elements.

fields.title: Pride and Prejudice
fields.author: Jane Austen
fields.description: Pride and Prejudice is a romantic novel by Jane Austen that follows Elizabeth Bennet as she deals with issues of manners, upbringing, morality, and marriage in early 19th-century England.

fields.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
fields.author: Harper Lee
fields.description: To Kill a Mockingbird is a novel by Harper Lee set in the American South during the 1930s. It follows young Scout Finch whose father Atticus defends a Black man falsely accused of a crime.
